sources.name: National Register of Historic Places 1984 nomination: A.E. Larson Building, section 7 architectural description
sources.holder: US National Park Service / National Register of Historic Places

rights.reuse: Use as documentary reference; verify any original photos or reproduced archival designs separately.

sources.notes: 1984 description records original seven ground-floor shop entrances (four on Second Street, three on Yakima Avenue); three corner storefronts altered in 1963 for a bank; 65 x 130 ft footprint and 188 ft height to flagpole; salmon brick and varied stone/metal finishes. The report is retrospective evidence, not a 1960 photograph.

claims.assertion: The A.E. Larson Building was constructed in 1931.
John W. Maloney designed an Art Deco office building at 6 S. 2nd St.

claims.reason: Built 1931 and registered in 1984; specific 1960 survey is not yet attached.

claims.assertion: The current prototype's facade, signage and dimensions match the 1960 building.
claims.reason: No direct 1960 facade source or measurements validated.

claims.assertion: The City of Yakima's self-guided historic downtown walking-tour map numbers Larson Building as stop 27 near South Second Street and Yakima Avenue.
The Larson Building's corner shop fronts were remodeled in 1963 into one large bank rental unit; the alteration affected three of the seven original shop fronts.
In 1960 the corner shop fronts predated the alterations documented as occurring in 1963, and the original multi-shop arrangement is a defensible historical reconstruction.
claims.reason: Retrospective 1984 NPS nomination dates alterations to 1963. Exact 1960 storefront occupancy, glazing variations and dimensions have not been directly checked.

claims.assertion: The 1984 NRHP nomination describes the Larson Building as 65 feet by 130 feet, with a height of 188 feet to the top of the flagpole.
The 1984 NRHP nomination describes salmon-colored brick, decorative bronze and stone details, original separate Second Street and Yakima Avenue shop entrances, and surviving Art Deco details.

promotionGates.rule: Do not label a scene element 'verified 1960' based only on a 1920/1950 map or construction date.
Do not label massing or geo coordinates exact until a date-valid georeferenced source establishes them.
Do not embed archival imagery unless item-level publication rights are recorded.
Resolve Capitol Theatre 9 vs 19 South Third address conflict before exact address geocoding.
Integrate as metadata into canonical Evercraft Worlds engine; do not fork renderer, movement, save, or physics.
Display documented, interval-inferred, illustrative and unresolved clearly in user-facing provenance.
A source that merely says 'Yakima Avenue' is inadmissible for Yakima, Washington without verified city, state and country. Reject Seattle and Tacoma Yakima street-name collisions.
A documented claim dated 1960 must cite a directly dated, individually identifiable 1960 item matching Yakima, WA; a 1959/1961 pair is still an inference.
